# Temple Scroll Column 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 17 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**17:1** And he shall not multiply for himself wives, and they shall not turn his heart away from Me.

**17:2** And silver and gold he shall not greatly multiply for himself.

**17:3** And when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him this torah

**17:4** upon a scroll, from before the priests, the Levites.

**17:5** And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life,

**17:6** so that he may learn to fear Me, and to keep all the words of this torah

**17:7** and these statutes, to do them.

**17:8** So that his heart shall not be lifted up above his brothers, and so that he shall not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left,

**17:9** in order that he may prolong his days over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

**17:10** vacat

**17:11** And you shall take for the ordination: one young bull and one ram from the flock,

**17:12** and unleavened bread and unleavened cakes mixed with oil and unleavened wafers anointed with oil;

**17:13** of fine wheat flour you shall make them.

**17:14** And you shall put them upon one basket and bring them near in the basket,

**17:15** and the bull and the two rams.

**17:16** And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

---

*EMET notes: Column 17 is well preserved. Lines 1-9 complete the Law of the King from Column 16, paralleling Deuteronomy 17:17-20. The prohibitions against multiplying wives, silver, and gold — and the requirement to write and study the torah scroll — are central to the Temple Scroll's vision of limited monarchy. After a vacat, lines 11-16 begin the ordination (millu'im) instructions, paralleling Exodus 29:1-4. "Torah" preserved untranslated as a key theological term.*
